## Glossary

**apiTokens**  
Setting that opts in to API-key providers and the API decision provider (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); cannot combine with subscriptionOnly.

**assertMainThreadLabs**  
Throws unless every registered main thread runs on a main-thread lab.

**Cheap models for decisions**  
Wardens (advise, guard and review) run Claude Haiku 5.5, the default Layer 2 Sonnet 5.5 low; only the Artificer uses a capable model by default.

**Codex worker CODEX_HOME**  
A Codex worker runs on a Foundry-private .foundry/runtime-profiles/<source id>/codex-home linking the profile's auth.json.

**defaults.nativeAuthenticationId**  
Optional explicit native-profile source for the worker; its runtime matches the worker.

**defaults.provider**  
The main-thread worker harness: claude-code (default) or codex without API tokens.

**FOUNDRY_STARTUP_SELF_TEST**  
Env flag (=1) that lets startup make one decision call; not run while project Warden hosts run (each host's start proves the decision login).

**Integration limits**  
Local profile references are not Kingdom capacity grants; an execution contract must authorize roles, models and budgets itself.

**main thread**  
The default worker and every enabled executor; may run only on a main-thread lab.

**MAIN_THREAD_LABS**  
The five labs main threads may run on (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI); others, gateways and local hosts are refused.

**native-profile source**  
A nativeAuthentication entry naming a private (0700) profile directory: a credential reference, never a token.

**refused setting**  
A setting subscription mode cannot enforce (a non-subscription worker, an executor on another provider, a main-thread model the worker does not run, learning.review provider/model overrides) is refused.

**resolveSubscriptionPolicy**  
Resolves subscription mode (default) versus API tokens, checking login locations at startup.

**shared holder**  
The worker and decisions may both hold one login, like the user's own concurrent CLI sessions.

**Subscription-only default**  
No API provider, no paid fallback, no automatic retry, no model substitution unless apiTokens is set.

**subscription-policy**  
Class: subscription-only by default, apiTokens opt-in, which login and model the worker and each role use, integration limits.

**subscriptionOnly.decisionSourceId**  
Optional explicit native-profile source for decisions; must match decisionRuntime when both are set.

**subscriptionSettingsSchema**  
Validates the optional subscription-mode overrides, each with a default.

**workerModelRequirement**  
Says why a model cannot run on the subscription worker, or undefined when it can.

## 1. What this Warden covers

The policy that Foundry is subscription-only by default: the worker and every decision role run on the logins already on the machine, API-key providers exist only behind the apiTokens opt-in, and the policy decides which login, harness and model each role may use.

## 2. The domain

A fresh install with no settings runs the Claude Code worker on the default Claude login (~/.claude) and every decision role on Claude Haiku 5.5 through the same login. resolveSubscriptionPolicy resolves the mode at startup and checks the login locations: in subscription mode no API provider is constructed, and there is no paid fallback, no automatic retry and no model substitution. `apiTokens: true` is the only opt-in to API-key providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, gateways, Kingdom bindings) and cannot be combined with `subscriptionOnly`. `defaults.provider` picks the worker harness (`claude-code`, or `codex` on the Codex CLI's ChatGPT login); `defaults.nativeAuthenticationId` and `subscriptionOnly.decisionSourceId` name explicit native-profile sources for the worker and the decisions (credential references, never tokens; the decision source must match the decision runtime). The worker and decisions may share one login as shared holders; gateways, Kingdom bindings and per-thread authentication selections cannot be mixed in. subscriptionSettingsSchema validates the optional overrides with their defaults.

Models: main threads run only on the five labs in MAIN_THREAD_LABS (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI), checked by assertMainThreadLabs; a Codex worker must be a ChatGPT login and runs on its own Foundry-private CODEX_HOME. An executor, project or thread may choose any model the subscription worker runs (workerModelRequirement says why one cannot). Decision roles are different: cheap models decide, capable models work, so a role cannot choose its model: every first-stage decision runs on its runtime's decision login host, which launches with the decision model and refuses a call naming any other, and a later classify stage on another model runs on that stage's own host; settings that cannot be enforced (an executor on another provider, a main-thread model the worker does not run, learning.review provider/model overrides) are refused. Local profile references are not Kingdom capacity grants, and startup makes no model calls unless FOUNDRY_STARTUP_SELF_TEST=1 (and not even then while project Warden hosts run).

Not here: how decisions actually run (the decision login host, the primed pool, the scheduler, budgets, deadlines, the decision runtime and decision model settings, receipts) is the `decision-hosts` region; Wardens held in one Claude Code process per project (the project Warden host) are `in-session-wardens`; login profile directories, credential sources, Kingdom-held logins and private files are `logins-secrets`; the model registry and API-key providers themselves are `models-providers`; launching the worker session is `native-sessions`; Kingdom capacity grants are `kingdom`; the settings file and its patch semantics are `settings-runtime`.

**Source:** `docs/subscription-decisions.md` § (preface) (in "Subscription-only Foundry")

### Subscription-only Foundry

Foundry runs subscription-only by default. A fresh install, with no settings at all, runs the Claude Code worker and Foundry's decisions from the logins already on the machine:

- **Worker:** Claude Code, using the default Claude login (`~/.claude`, selected by leaving `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` unset). Set `defaults.provider` to `codex` (for example with `defaults.model: "gpt-6.2-astra"`) to run main threads on Codex by default instead, on the Codex CLI's ChatGPT login (`~/.codex`). A project may set its own default (`projects[id].defaults.provider`), and any thread may start on another worker (below).
- **Decisions:** Claude Haiku 5.5 (`claude-haiku-5-5`) through the same Claude login (`~/.claude`), with every Warden of a project held warm in one Foundry-owned Claude Code process per project (the project Warden host, below). Wardens (advise, guard and review) use this decision profile; a thread's first name is its first message's words, with no decision call. The runtime is a setting: `subscriptionOnly.decisionRuntime: "claude"` keeps every Warden on primed Claude Code sessions, and `"codex"` runs decisions on the Codex CLI's ChatGPT login (`~/.codex`) with GPT-6 Luna instead.

No API provider is constructed in this mode. There is no paid fallback, no automatic retry and no model substitution. API-key providers need an explicit opt-in.

<!-- unit doc:docs/subscription-decisions.md#settings -->
**Source:** `docs/subscription-decisions.md` § Settings (in "Subscription-only Foundry")

#### Settings

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `apiTokens` | absent (`false`) | `true` opts in to API-key providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, gateways, Kingdom bindings) and the API decision provider, Anthropic Haiku 5.5 by default, which requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. It cannot be combined with `subscriptionOnly`. |
| `defaults.provider` | `claude-code` | The default main-thread worker (a project's `defaults.provider` overrides it). Without API tokens it is a subscription harness: `claude-code` or `codex`. |
| `defaults.nativeAuthenticationId` | absent: each runtime's first configured `native-profile` source, else `~/.claude` or `~/.codex` | Names a runtime's primary login. Every configured `native-profile` source of a runtime is a login of its worker, except the decision source (`subscriptionOnly.decisionSourceId`, the Wardens' login) unless it is also the named primary; several are a pool, balanced (below). With none configured besides the decision source, the worker runs on the default location. Naming a Codex source never moves the Claude worker to `~/.claude`. |
| `subscriptionPools.<claude\|codex>` | absent: `quartile-balanced`, balancing on | How a runtime with several logins balances them (below): `routing` (`quartile-balanced`, `owner-first`, `priority-balanced`), `preferredLoginId` (the login `owner-first` prefers and pinning runs on) and `pinned` (`true` is balancing off: every launch runs on the preferred login; the routing is kept for when it is turned back on). A project's `projects[id].subscriptionPools` overrides it for that project's threads. |
| `defaults.decisionProvider` / `decisionModel` | `subscription-decisions` / `claude-haiku-5-5` | New configurations record the decision profile here; `decisionModel` selects the decision model. A model registered only on the other runtime is refused rather than substituted. |
| `subscriptionOnly.decisionRuntime` | absent: Claude decisions, Wardens in project hosts | Decision runtime when no explicit source is named. Absent or `claude-project`: Claude decisions (`~/.claude`), every Warden of a project held warm in one Foundry-owned Claude Code process per project, asked for advice by every thread of the project, whatever its worker (below). `claude`: Claude decisions with every Warden on its own primed session (the evals' baseline). `codex`: Codex decisions (`~/.codex`), primed Wardens. |
| `subscriptionOnly.projectHost` | absent: the defaults below | Project hosts only (refused with `claude` or Codex decisions): `sparesPerWarden` (1), `wardensPerDispatcher` (8: the most Wardens one dispatcher holds. The number of dispatchers is one while the roster fits a single slice, else the square root of the roster rounded up, never more than this many Wardens each and never more than 24 dispatchers: 6 for 32 Wardens, 8 for 64, 10 for 75, 14 for 106; `dispatcherCount`. Each dispatcher refills its slice at once; one dispatcher took ~20 s to refill 75), `concurrentTurns` (2), `maxRssMb` (1536), `hardRssMb` (4096), `maxRecyclesPerHour` (20), `recycleTokens` (140000), `setupDeadlineMs` (30 s + 0.6 s per held spare), `restartBackoffMs` (5000), `maxRestarts` (5), `idleMs` (3 hours). See "Project Warden host". |
| `subscriptionOnly.decisionSourceId` | absent: the runtime's default login | Optional explicit `native-profile` source for decisions. It must match `decisionRuntime` when both are set. |
| `subscriptionOnly.model` | `claude-haiku-5-5` for Claude, `gpt-5.6-luna` for Codex (a ChatGPT login on an older Codex CLI, 0.153.4, is refused `gpt-6-luna`) | Decision model; overrides `decisionModel`. Heavier roles can name `claude-opus-5-5` or `claude-fable-5-1`. |
| `subscriptionOnly.expectedObservedModel` | the requested model | Claude decision profiles only: the id the CLI must report serving (for example the full id behind an alias). Codex does not acknowledge a different model. |
| `subscriptionOnly.directory` | `<project>/.foundry/decision-receipts` | Private (0700) receipt directory. The default is created at startup; an explicit directory must already exist and be private. Receipts only: the decision sessions run in the host's working folder (below). |
| `subscriptionOnly.maxCalls` | `10000` | Finite decision attempt budget for this Foundry process, including failed admitted attempts. It does not renew automatically. |
| `subscriptionOnly.maxConcurrent` | `16` | Decisions running at once across all threads: Claude CLI processes (~130–230 MB each), or concurrent turns on the one warm Codex process. Sized for a full chorus: every Warden is asked on every user message, and every guard-triggered Warden on every action. |
| (primed keys) | `2 × Wardens + 8`, at least 16 | With `decisionRuntime: "claude"` only (with project hosts no pool is built): Claude decision roles kept primed, sized at startup from the largest chorus any project runs (its region Wardens; an advice and a review key each). Each holds a spare CLI process (~130–230 MB): 25 Wardens is about 50 processes and 10 GB. An evicted key re-primes cold (5–8 s). Not a setting. |
| `subscriptionOnly.maxQueued` | `512` | Waiting decisions across all threads (up to 1024). |
| `subscriptionOnly.maxQueuedPerThread` | `256` | Waiting decisions per logical thread: deep enough that a burst of guards never refuses admission. |
| `subscriptionOnly.effort` | `low` | Decision reasoning effort (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`; Haiku 5.5 accepts `low` to `high`). The model default, `medium`, adds latency per decision. |
| `subscriptionOnly.hedgeAfterMs` | `4000` for Codex | A decision still running after this long starts the same input on a second branch; the first to finish wins (500 to 30000). |
| `subscriptionOnly.callTimeoutMs` | `60000` | Per-decision deadline including queue and preflight time (100 to 120000). |

Explicit profile sources are credential references in `nativeAuthentication`, never tokens:

```json
{
  "nativeAuthentication": [
    { "id": "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222", "integrationId": "44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444",
      "runtime": "codex", "mode": "native-profile", "profileDirectory": "/private/path/decisions" }
  ],
  "subscriptionOnly": { "decisionSourceId": "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222" }
}
```

An explicit profile directory must be an owned private (0700) directory with private files. The default login locations are referenced in place: they must be owned, real directories whose credential files (`auth.json`, `.credentials.json`) are private, but Foundry does not require or change their mode. The worker and the decisions may share one login: both are shared holders of it, like the user's own concurrent CLI sessions. Gateways, Kingdom bindings and per-thread authentication selections cannot be mixed into subscription mode.

<!-- unit doc:docs/subscription-decisions.md#main-threads -->
**Source:** `docs/subscription-decisions.md` § Main threads (in "Subscription-only Foundry")

#### Main threads

Main threads (the default worker and every enabled executor) run on models from five labs: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta and xAI (`MAIN_THREAD_LABS` in the core model registry). Other labs, gateways and local hosts are refused as main threads in every mode. How each lab runs:

| Lab | Subscription (default) | With `apiTokens: true` |
|---|---|---|
| Anthropic | `claude-code` on the Claude login | also `anthropic` (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) |
| OpenAI | `codex` on the Codex ChatGPT login | also `openai` (`OPENAI_API_KEY`) |
| Google | no harness yet (agent-session's ACP transport for Gemini CLI is a stub) | `gemini` (`GEMINI_API_KEY`) |
| Meta | no harness yet | `meta` (`MODEL_API_KEY`) |
| xAI | no harness yet | `xai` (`XAI_API_KEY`) |

A refused main thread names what it needs, in the settings API, the viewer's Defaults editor and setup.

A Codex worker is checked with `codex login status` and must be a ChatGPT login; an API-key login is refused. It shares the Codex login with Codex decisions (both are shared holders, so they may use the same `~/.codex`) and runs on its own Foundry-private `CODEX_HOME` (`.foundry/runtime-profiles/<source id>/codex-home`, kept across restarts so sessions resume) that links the profile's `auth.json`. None of the user's Codex config, instructions or MCP servers apply to it, and it runs with Codex's own sandbox and approvals off, like the Claude worker's bypass mode.

<!-- unit doc:docs/subscription-decisions.md#existing-settings -->
**Source:** `docs/subscription-decisions.md` § Existing settings (in "Subscription-only Foundry")

#### Existing settings

Subscription mode sets the decision defaults (`defaults.decisionProvider`, `defaults.decisionModel`) to the decision profile. The saved settings file is not rewritten. Settings that cannot be enforced are refused: a worker that is not a subscription harness, an executor on another provider, a main-thread model the worker does not run, and `learning.review` provider/model overrides.

The default model is only the default. An executor (`agents[id].model`), a project (`projects[id].defaults.model`) and a thread (the launch settings a host or the viewer chooses) may each run any model its subscription worker runs, as its registry entry lists them (`workerModelRequirement`); a model of another provider is refused. Decision roles are different: a role cannot choose its model. Every first-stage decision runs on its runtime's decision login host (its project Warden hosts by default; the primed pool with `decisionRuntime` `claude` or `codex`), which launches with the decision model and refuses a call naming any other; a later classify stage on another model or effort (the default Layer 2, Sonnet 5.5 low) runs on that stage's own decision host, launched with the stage's model (with project hosts, its own per-project lane).

<!-- unit doc:docs/subscription-decisions.md#integration-limits -->
**Source:** `docs/subscription-decisions.md` § Integration limits (in "Subscription-only Foundry")

#### Integration limits

Local profile references are not Kingdom capacity grants. A project execution contract must independently authorize worker and decision roles, purposes, model identities, aggregate budgets, deadlines and generation revocation. Startup makes no model calls unless `FOUNDRY_STARTUP_SELF_TEST=1` is set. With project Warden hosts the self-test is not run: each host's start proves the decision login (`claude auth status`, then its setup turn). Otherwise (API-token decisions, `decisionRuntime: "claude"` or `"codex"`) it makes one decision call.

<!-- unit doc:CLAUDE.md#model-routing -->
**Source:** `CLAUDE.md` § Model Routing (in "Foundry")

#### Model Routing

**Cheap models for decisions, capable models for work.** Wardens (advise, guard and review) and the feedback lifecycle run on Claude Haiku 5.5 (`claude-haiku-5-5`). Heavier reasoning roles use Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) or Fable 5.2 (`claude-fable-5-2`). Only the Artificer uses a capable model by default.

Foundry is subscription-only by default and all Claude for now (2026-10-11): the Artificer runs on the Claude Code login (`~/.claude`) by default (Codex, with `defaults.provider: "codex"`, is a setting; a project may set its own default worker, and any thread may start on another worker it has a login for, stored on the thread and never changed silently: FEAT-007; an idle thread may switch worker mid-conversation, continuing on a fresh session seeded from its journal behind a `worker-switch` marker; the thread also holds its exact model, an alias pinned to the id it points to, changed only by `changeThreadModel` behind a "Switched to" marker, and a retired model moves only open threads, to the newest of its family on the same worker, while a thread revived from archive on one asks for a model: `models/model-succession.ts`), and every decision role runs Claude Haiku 5.5 through the same Claude login, with no API provider constructed and no paid fallback. The decision runtime and model are settings (`subscriptionOnly.decisionRuntime`, `subscriptionOnly.model` / `defaults.decisionModel`), so Codex or another lab can run decisions again without code changes. **The per-project host is the only Warden runtime** (Aron, 2026-11-03: "the Claude project is the only thing that actually makes sense"): with Claude decisions (no `decisionRuntime`, or `claude-project`), every Warden of a project is held warm in one Foundry-owned Claude Code process per project (`providers/project-warden-hosts.ts`), on the decision login, only while someone works in the project (opened by a turn or by a thread of it created or opened, closed after `projectHost.idleMs` idle, 3 hours by default; a turn never waits for it: a user message's advice to a Warden it holds no warm spare for, or whose host does not serve, is skipped, never started cold, and catches up on the thread's next message (`agents/warden-catch-up.ts`, the cursor rebuilt from the journal on restore), asked on the user messages it missed since it last answered, capped at five or about 4k tokens with a count of the rest), composed at the project root and stateless (the thread's part rides with the moment); every thread of the project, on any worker, sends its advice there. Guards, reviews and later stages go to the host too, a later stage on another model to its own per-project lane (#420). **No host serving, no Warden call** (Aron, 2026-11-18: "it should not be handling warden calls at all"): while a project's host is starting, failed or closed, its Wardens' first-stage calls are refused unsent (`projectHostTarget`, `not-held`), never sent to primed; a user message's advice catches up as above, and a guard, review, brief, consumed item, milestone, hand-back or Retry is not sent and shows as not started. A host is replaced blue/green past its memory and recycle bounds and restarted with backoff (`subscriptionOnly.projectHost`). A later stage whose lane does not serve is skipped the same way, and the Warden says nothing at that moment: Layer 1's unconfirmed yes never stands in for it (classify `runStages`; Aron, 2026-11-18: "when the layers are down, they just skip"). In this mode the daemon builds no primed pool (`createDecisionLoginHost`, `providers/decision-login-host.ts`, holds the decision login, its used-up pause, the receipts and the host launcher; the pool, `createPrimedPool`, is built only for `claude` and `codex`), and no daemon caller would need one: a thread's first name is its first message's words, and the opt-in startup self-test is not run while project hosts are (each host's start proves the decision login); the daemon wires no feedback classifier, so `/correction` is recorded as said (chorus `docs/RETIRE-PRIMED-POOL.md`). `decisionRuntime: "claude"` keeps every Warden primed (the evals' baseline); `codex` runs decisions on Codex, Wardens primed. API-key providers require `apiTokens: true`; their decision default is Anthropic Haiku 5.5. Main threads run on Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta and xAI models only. See [subscription decisions](docs/subscription-decisions.md) for settings, bounds and ownership.
